theory.intro: A **radial survey** measures land from one central point, recording the true bearing and distance to each corner. Joining each corner to the next splits the land into triangles that all meet at the centre.
facts: The angle at the centre between two radials is the difference of their true bearings.
When the pair straddles north, add the part before north to the part after it: from $310^{\circ}$ to $040^{\circ}$ is $50^{\circ}+40^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$.
The angles at the centre must add to $360^{\circ}$, so check that before going any further.
Each triangle's area is $A=\tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two radials and $C$ is the angle between them.
The total area of the land is the sum of the areas of all the triangles.
Each boundary length comes from the cosine rule $c=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}-2ab\cos C}$.
steps: Find every angle at the centre from the bearings
Check the angles add to 360 degrees
Apply the area rule or the cosine rule to each triangle
Add the results to give the total area or perimeter

foundation.solution_text:
The radials $OD$ and $OA$ lie either side of north, so add the two parts.
$\angle DOA=(360^{\circ}-310^{\circ})+40^{\circ}$
$=90^{\circ}$
$A=\tfrac{1}{2}(28)(30)\sin 90^{\circ}$
$=420\text{ m}^{2}$

The radials $OP$ and $OQ$ lie either side of north, so add the two parts.
$\angle POQ=(360^{\circ}-335^{\circ})+42^{\circ}$
$=67^{\circ}$
$A=\tfrac{1}{2}(54)(61)\sin 67^{\circ}$
$=1516.0714\ldots$
$\approx 1516.1\text{ m}^{2}$

The radials $OU$ and $OV$ lie either side of north, so add the two parts.
$\angle UOV=(360^{\circ}-300^{\circ})+55^{\circ}$
$=115^{\circ}$
$UV=\sqrt{25^{2}+32^{2}-2(25)(32)\cos 115^{\circ}}$
$=\sqrt{2325.1892\ldots}$
$=48.2202\ldots$
$\approx 48.2\text{ m}$

The radials $OZ$ and $OX$ lie either side of north, so add the two parts.
$\angle ZOX=(360^{\circ}-262^{\circ})+25^{\circ}$
$=123^{\circ}$
$ZX=\sqrt{38^{2}+44^{2}-2(38)(44)\cos 123^{\circ}}$
$=\sqrt{5201.2725\ldots}$
$=72.1198\ldots$
$\approx 72.1\text{ m}$

development.solution_text:
1. **Find every angle at the centre from the bearings**
$\angle AOB=137^{\circ}-18^{\circ}=119^{\circ}$
$\angle BOC=254^{\circ}-137^{\circ}=117^{\circ}$
$\angle COA=(360^{\circ}-254^{\circ})+18^{\circ}=124^{\circ}$
2. **Check the angles add to 360 degrees**
$119^{\circ}+117^{\circ}+124^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$
3. **Apply the area rule or the cosine rule to each triangle**
$A_{AOB}=\tfrac{1}{2}(26)(31)\sin 119^{\circ}=352.4717\ldots$
$A_{BOC}=\tfrac{1}{2}(31)(23)\sin 117^{\circ}=317.6438\ldots$
$A_{COA}=\tfrac{1}{2}(23)(26)\sin 124^{\circ}=247.8822\ldots$
4. **Add the results to give the total area or perimeter**
$A=352.4717\ldots+317.6438\ldots+247.8822\ldots$
$=917.9977\ldots$
$\approx 918.0\text{ m}^{2}$

1. **Find every angle at the centre from the bearings**
$\angle DOE=195^{\circ}-72^{\circ}=123^{\circ}$
$\angle EOF=320^{\circ}-195^{\circ}=125^{\circ}$
$\angle FOD=(360^{\circ}-320^{\circ})+72^{\circ}=112^{\circ}$
2. **Check the angles add to 360 degrees**
$123^{\circ}+125^{\circ}+112^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$
3. **Apply the area rule or the cosine rule to each triangle**
$DE=\sqrt{45^{2}+52^{2}-2(45)(52)\cos 123^{\circ}}=85.3106\ldots$
$EF=\sqrt{52^{2}+38^{2}-2(52)(38)\cos 125^{\circ}}=80.0922\ldots$
$FD=\sqrt{38^{2}+45^{2}-2(38)(45)\cos 112^{\circ}}=68.9213\ldots$
4. **Add the results to give the total area or perimeter**
$P=85.3106\ldots+80.0922\ldots+68.9213\ldots$
$=234.3243\ldots$
$\approx 234\text{ m}$

1. **Find every angle at the centre from the bearings**
$\angle POQ=105^{\circ}-32^{\circ}=73^{\circ}$
$\angle QOR=198^{\circ}-105^{\circ}=93^{\circ}$
$\angle ROS=295^{\circ}-198^{\circ}=97^{\circ}$
$\angle SOP=(360^{\circ}-295^{\circ})+32^{\circ}=97^{\circ}$
2. **Check the angles add to 360 degrees**
$73^{\circ}+93^{\circ}+97^{\circ}+97^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$
3. **Apply the area rule or the cosine rule to each triangle**
$A_{POQ}=\tfrac{1}{2}(58)(64)\sin 73^{\circ}=1774.9016\ldots$
$A_{QOR}=\tfrac{1}{2}(64)(49)\sin 93^{\circ}=1565.8511\ldots$
$A_{ROS}=\tfrac{1}{2}(49)(71)\sin 97^{\circ}=1726.5340\ldots$
$A_{SOP}=\tfrac{1}{2}(71)(58)\sin 97^{\circ}=2043.6525\ldots$
4. **Add the results to give the total area or perimeter**
$A=1774.9016\ldots+1565.8511\ldots+1726.5340\ldots+2043.6525\ldots$
$=7110.9392\ldots$
$\approx 7111\text{ m}^{2}$

1. **Find every angle at the centre from the bearings**
$\angle JOK=100^{\circ}-15^{\circ}=85^{\circ}$
$\angle KOL=190^{\circ}-100^{\circ}=90^{\circ}$
$\angle LOM=288^{\circ}-190^{\circ}=98^{\circ}$
$\angle MOJ=(360^{\circ}-288^{\circ})+15^{\circ}=87^{\circ}$
2. **Check the angles add to 360 degrees**
$85^{\circ}+90^{\circ}+98^{\circ}+87^{\circ}=360^{\circ}$
3. **Apply the area rule or the cosine rule to each triangle**
$JK=\sqrt{40^{2}+55^{2}-2(40)(55)\cos 85^{\circ}}=65.1269\ldots$
$KL=\sqrt{55^{2}+47^{2}-2(55)(47)\cos 90^{\circ}}=72.3463\ldots$
$LM=\sqrt{47^{2}+62^{2}-2(47)(62)\cos 98^{\circ}}=82.8498\ldots$
$MJ=\sqrt{62^{2}+40^{2}-2(62)(40)\cos 87^{\circ}}=72.0028\ldots$
4. **Add the results to give the total area or perimeter**
$P=65.1269\ldots+72.3463\ldots+82.8498\ldots+72.0028\ldots$
$=292.3260\ldots$
$\approx 292\text{ m}$
